title: Can you add an open question to this idea?

messages.text: Can you add an open question to this idea?

context.label: DDIM-NLL: likelihood from the DDIM trajectory via instantaneous change-of-variables
context.digest: Attach a Hutchinson-trace change-of-variables term to the DDIM steps already taken during sampling, so negative log-likelihood comes at the marginal cost of one Jacobian-vector product per step.

plan.goal: Add one new open question to the selected DDIM-NLL idea.

args.instruction: The selected idea, 'DDIM-NLL: likelihood from the DDIM trajectory via instantaneous change-of-variables', already carries six open questions: (1) invariance of the accumulated log-Jacobian and its Hutchinson variance across ε/v/score parameterizations of the same continuous drift; (2) whether DDIM's Euler discretization bias corrupts the change-of-variables estimate and what it converges to as T grows; (3) whether a trajectory-distilled velocity inherits or corrects that bias and whether its accumulated log-Jacobian matches the log-|det| of the learned map; (4) how many Hutchinson projections are needed and whether the per-step vjp beats a fine-grained ODE solve at equal accuracy; (5) whether the divergence should accumulate along the pure deterministic path or a predictor–corrector variant; (6) whether the resulting NLL is comparable to DDPM/Score-SDE numbers given DDIM's marginal is defined by the discretized map. Add exactly ONE new open question not covered by any of these. It should be genuinely open (not settled by the idea's own argument), empirically answerable, and consequential for whether the estimator is trustworthy or worth deploying. Good hunting grounds: threats the existing six miss — e.g. high-curvature regions where the linearized Jacobian or the Hutchinson estimate breaks down; sensitivity to the choice of DDIM schedule or σ_t; behavior under guidance (e.g. CFG) or distilled samplers; validity when x_T is off the N(0,I) manifold; whether the estimate is biased in a known direction (over- or under-estimating NLL) and in which regime. Do not restate or re-wrap any existing question. Return the single open question, phrased precisely, plus one or two sentences on why answering it matters.

steps.why: Adding an open question to a selected idea is refinement of that idea, not new research — one skeptic pass, no literature lookup.

done_criteria: the returned open question is distinct from all six already listed on the idea

messages.text: I added a seventh open question to the idea, alongside the six already there. The new one asks whether the change-of-variables NLL remains valid under classifier-free guidance, where the effective drift $v + w \cdot (v_c - v_{unc})$ is no longer the probability-flow field of any normalized distribution — so the accumulated log-Jacobian may be systematically over- or under-confident in a way that grows with the guidance weight. It is distinct from the existing six, which all assume the single unguided drift, and it is the regime DDIM is actually deployed in (e.g., Stable Diffusion). It is empirically answerable by accumulating the trace along the guided trajectory and comparing against a fine-grained ODE solve on that same guided field.

plan.goal: Add a classifier guidance section to the DDIM-NLL idea.

args.instruction: Add a proper 'classifier guidance' section to this idea, distinct from the classifier-free guidance (CFG) material already present. Cover: the classifier-guided effective drift (e.g., v + s·∇_x log p(y|x) at each step, where the guidance signal is an external classifier's gradient), how that drift changes the accumulated log-Jacobian in the change-of-variables estimator, whether the NLL estimate remains valid — or what it actually estimates — under a drift that is not the probability-flow field of the true data distribution, how the classifier-guidance regime differs from the CFG regime already discussed (separate gradient source, guidance scale s vs. weight w, the role of the classifier's accuracy/calibration), and any empirical checks for validating the estimate under classifier guidance. Integrate it as a coherent section of the idea write-up rather than a separate note, and make clear how it relates to the existing open question about CFG.

steps.why: The user wants the selected idea expanded with a classifier guidance section — refinement of the idea in hand, not new candidates or new literature.

the revised candidate contains a classifier guidance section distinct from the existing CFG material
